newsitem.title: USA: AT&T in preliminary pact with HFS.
newsitem.headline: AT&T in preliminary pact with HFS.

text.p: AT&T Corp and HFS Inc said on Thursday they have entered a preliminary agreement for AT&T to market residential long distance service to current and future customers of HFS's real estate brands.
The companies said the deal is expected extend AT&T's reach in the consumer telephone service business, while providing recurring revenues to HFS.

HFS is the parent company of Century 21, Coldwell Banker and ERA residential real estate franchises representing 100,000 residential real estate broker-owners and agents at 11,200 franchise offices, the companies said.
Outlined in the letter of intent is a plan for HFS to market AT&T residential long distance service and calling plans including the flagship calling plan AT&T One Rate, the companies said.
The arrangement is subject to AT&T and HFS entering into a formal contract, the companies said.
AT&T had previously announced that it wanted to to broaden its consumer marketing channels. AT&T has reached marketing agreements with ADT Ltd in March and Shaklee Corp in November 1996.
Shaklee, a direct marketer of nutritional supplements, personal care products and householder cleaners, is a unit of Japan's Yamanouchi Pharmaceutical Co Ltd. Shaklee has 500,000 sales agents.

AT&T has said that it intends to cut back on the practice of issuing checks to lure and retain customers. The new marketing alliances also aim to get its services to customers without the use of telemarketers, a method that tends to annoy customers.

In a separate deal, HFS and AT&T Wireless Services said the companies entered a four-year agreement for AT&T to provide the best rate plan available for franchisees and employees of HFS's real estate brands, eight hotel brands, Avis rental car system and to developers of Resort Condominiums International.
